manual.title: PV site
manual.description: A site is one location. After creating it, add its inverters and then its panel arrays.

data_description.interval: 15 minutes uses Open-Meteo's 15-minute data (native in Central Europe).
data_description.beam_mode: "Sub-steps" averages sun angle and shading every 7.5 minutes; "Like the app" calculates exactly as solXpect does.

import_app.title: Import from solXpect
import_app.description: Upload the backup ZIP that the solXpect app exports (it contains databases/SQLITE.db).

import_select.title: Choose the plants
import_select.description: Plants without "central inverter" get their own inverter; plants with "central inverter" share one inverter whose limit is the sum of their limits. All chosen plants must have the same location. If the plants in the app are alternative variants of the same installation, choose only one.

error.invalid_backup: This file couldn't be read as a solXpect backup.
error.different_locations: The chosen plants have different locations. Import them as separate sites.

data_description.site: Choosing another site moves the inverter there, together with its panel arrays.

error.name_exists: An inverter with this name already exists.

user.title: Panel array
user.description: A group of panels with the same orientation, e.g. one string.

data_description.azimuth: Direction the panels face: 0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west.

data_description.inverter: Choosing an inverter of another site moves the array to that site.

panels.title: Orientation and size
panels.description: If you change azimuth or tilt, the shading step follows, because other directions may now be in front of the panel.

data_description.azimuth: Direction the panels face: 0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west.

data_description.cells_max_power: Sum of the panels' rated power (Wp) from the datasheet.
data_description.cooling_factor: Cell temperature = air temperature + factor × irradiance. Typical values: well cooled 0.020, free standing 0.0208, flat on roof 0.026, not so well cooled 0.0342 (default, as in the app), transparent PV 0.0455, facade integrated 0.0538, on sloped roof 0.0563. Modern high-efficiency panels run somewhat cooler.
data_description.diffuse_efficiency: Share of the diffuse sky light the panels receive; the default follows from the tilt.
data_description.albedo: Grass about 0.2, asphalt about 0.1, fresh snow 0.6–0.8.

shading.title: Shading
shading.description:
For each direction (0° = north, 90° = east, 180° = south): the elevation of obstacles in degrees, and how much of the direct light they block in %, written as **elevation/opacity**, e.g. `35/100` or `20/60`. A single number means an opaque obstacle (`35` = `35/100`); `0` means no obstacle.

Only directions where the sun can stand in front of the panel are listed. The highest sun elevation there during the year (obstacles above it don't matter):
{sun}

The other directions are prefilled as blocked (`90`) in the collapsed section.

When you change an array, its saved values are prefilled.
